\";\nprint(escape(unsafe)); // \"<script>alert('xss')</script>\"\n```\n\n### namespace(initial?): object\n\nCreates a namespace object for mutable state in templates.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `initial: object` - Optional initial values\n\n**Returns:** Namespace object\n\n```hemlock\nimport { namespace } from \"@stdlib/jinja\";\n\nlet ns = namespace({ count: 0, total: 100 });\n```\n\n## Examples\n\n### LLM Chat Template (Qwen3 Style)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { render, namespace } from \"@stdlib/jinja\";\n\nlet template = `\n{%- for message in messages -%}\n{%- if message.role == 'system' -%}\n<|im_start|>system\n{{ message.content }}<|im_end|>\n{%- elif message.role == 'user' -%}\n<|im_start|>user\n{{ message.content }}<|im_end|>\n{%- elif message.role == 'assistant' -%}\n<|im_start|>assistant\n{{ message.content }}<|im_end|>\n{%- endif -%}\n{%- endfor -%}\n<|im_start|>assistant\n`;\n\nlet messages = [\n { role: \"system\", content: \"You are a helpful assistant.\" },\n { role: \"user\", content: \"Hello!\" }\n];\n\nprint(render(template, { messages: messages }));\n```\n\n### Tool Calls with JSON\n\n```hemlock\nimport { render } from \"@stdlib/jinja\";\n\nlet template = `\n{%- if tools -%}\nAvailable tools:\n{%- for tool in tools %}\n{{ tool|tojson }}\n{%- endfor %}\n{%- endif -%}\n`;\n\nlet context = {\n tools: [\n { name: \"search\", description: \"Search the web\" },\n { name: \"calculate\", description: \"Perform math\" }\n ]\n};\n\nprint(render(template, context));\n```\n\n### HTML Template\n\n```hemlock\nimport { render } from \"@stdlib/jinja\";\n\nlet template = `\n\n{{ title }}\n\n

{{ heading|escape }}

\n {% if items %}\n
    \n {% for item in items %}\n
  • {{ loop.index }}. {{ item|escape }}
    • \n {% endfor %}\n
\n {% else %}\n

No items found.

\n {% endif %}\n\n\n`;\n\nlet context = {\n title: \"My Page\",\n heading: \"Welcome!\",\n items: [\"Apple\", \"Banana\", \"Cherry\"]\n};\n\nprint(render(template, context));\n```\n\n### Dynamic Content with Type Checks\n\n```hemlock\nimport { render } from \"@stdlib/jinja\";\n\nlet template = `\n{%- for content in message.content -%}\n{%- if content is string -%}\n{{ content }}\n{%- elif 'text' in content -%}\n{{ content.text }}\n{%- elif 'image' in content -%}\n[Image: {{ content.image }}]\n{%- endif -%}\n{%- endfor -%}\n`;\n\nlet context = {\n message: {\n content: [\n \"Hello, \",\n { text: \"world\" },\n { image: \"photo.jpg\" }\n ]\n }\n};\n\nprint(render(template, context));\n```\n\n## Compatibility Notes\n\nThis implementation supports most common Jinja2 features needed for LLM chat templates:\n\n**Supported:**\n- Variable interpolation with dot notation and array indexing\n- Expression evaluation (+, - operators)\n- Built-in filters (see Filters section)\n- `if`/`elif`/`else`/`endif` conditionals\n- `for`/`endfor` loops with `loop` variable\n- `set` variable assignment\n- `namespace()` for mutable state\n- Type tests with `is`\n- Property checks with `in`\n- Whitespace control (`{%-`, `-%}`, `{{-`, `-}}`)\n- Comments `{# ... #}`\n- String literals in expressions\n\n**Not Supported:**\n- Macros and blocks\n- Template inheritance (`extends`, `include`)\n- Raw blocks\n- Custom filters\n- Line statements (`#`)\n- Complex expressions beyond + and -\n\nFor complex logic, process your data in Hemlock before passing it to the template.\n"}, "Bibliothèque standard -> json": {"id": "stdlib-json", "content": "# JSON Module Documentation\n\nComprehensive JSON manipulation library for parsing, serialization, formatting, validation, and querying JSON data.\n\n## Import\n\n```hemlock\nimport { parse, stringify, pretty } from \"@stdlib/json\";\nimport * as json from \"@stdlib/json\";\n```\n\n## API Reference\n\n### Core Functions\n\n#### `parse(json_str: string)`\n\nParse JSON string to value. Wrapper around built-in `.deserialize()` with enhanced error messages.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { parse } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet obj = parse('{\"x\":10,\"y\":20}');\nprint(obj.x); // 10\n\nlet arr = parse('[1,2,3]');\nprint(arr.length); // 3\n\n// Error handling\ntry {\n let invalid = parse('{\"unclosed\"');\n} catch (e) {\n print(\"Parse error: \" + e);\n}\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `json_str` (string) - JSON string to parse\n\n**Returns:** Parsed value (object, array, string, number, bool, or null)\n\n**Throws:** Parse error if JSON is malformed\n\n---\n\n#### `stringify(value)`\n\nSerialize value to compact JSON string. Wrapper around built-in `.serialize()`.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { stringify } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet json = stringify({ name: \"Alice\", age: 30 });\nprint(json); // {\"name\":\"Alice\",\"age\":30}\n\nlet arr_json = stringify([1, 2, 3]);\nprint(arr_json); // [1,2,3]\n\n// Circular reference detection\nlet obj = {};\nobj.self = obj;\ntry {\n stringify(obj);\n} catch (e) {\n print(e); // \"serialize() detected circular reference\"\n}\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `value` - Value to serialize (object, array, primitives)\n\n**Returns:** JSON string (compact format)\n\n**Throws:** Error on circular references\n\n---\n\n#### `parse_file(path: string)`\n\nRead and parse JSON from file.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { parse_file } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet config = parse_file(\"config.json\");\nprint(config.database.host);\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `path` (string) - Path to JSON file\n\n**Returns:** Parsed value\n\n**Throws:** File I/O errors or parse errors\n\n---\n\n#### `stringify_file(path: string, value)`\n\nSerialize value and write to file (compact format).\n\n```hemlock\nimport { stringify_file } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet data = { users: [{ name: \"Alice\" }, { name: \"Bob\" }] };\nstringify_file(\"output.json\", data);\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `path` (string) - Output file path\n- `value` - Value to serialize\n\n**Returns:** null\n\n**Throws:** File I/O errors or serialization errors\n\n---\n\n### Pretty Printing\n\n#### `pretty(value, indent?)`\n\nFormat value as pretty-printed JSON with indentation.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { pretty } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet data = { name: \"Alice\", items: [1, 2, 3] };\n\n// Default 2-space indentation\nlet formatted = pretty(data);\nprint(formatted);\n/*\n{\n \"name\": \"Alice\",\n \"items\": [\n 1,\n 2,\n 3\n ]\n}\n*/\n\n// Custom 4-space indentation\nlet formatted4 = pretty(data, 4);\n\n// Tab indentation\nlet tabbed = pretty(data, \"\\t\");\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `value` - Value to format\n- `indent` (optional) - Number of spaces (i32) or string (e.g., \"\\t\")\n\n**Returns:** Formatted JSON string\n\n**Default:** 2 spaces\n\n---\n\n#### `pretty_file(path: string, value, indent?)`\n\nPretty-print value to file.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { pretty_file } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet config = { server: { port: 8080, host: \"localhost\" } };\npretty_file(\"config.json\", config, 2);\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `path` (string) - Output file path\n- `value` - Value to format\n- `indent` (optional) - Number of spaces or string\n\n**Returns:** null\n\n---\n\n### Path Access\n\n#### `get(obj, path: string, default_val?)`\n\nGet value by path using dot notation.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { get } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet doc = {\n user: {\n name: \"Alice\",\n address: { city: \"NYC\", zip: 10001 }\n },\n items: [1, 2, 3]\n};\n\n// Nested object access\nlet name = get(doc, \"user.name\"); // \"Alice\"\nlet city = get(doc, \"user.address.city\"); // \"NYC\"\n\n// Array access (numeric indices)\nlet first = get(doc, \"items.0\"); // 1\nlet second = get(doc, \"items.1\"); // 2\n\n// Default value for missing paths\nlet phone = get(doc, \"user.phone\", \"(none)\"); // \"(none)\"\n\n// Empty path returns root\nlet root = get(doc, \"\"); // doc\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `obj` - Root object to query\n- `path` (string) - Dot-separated path (e.g., \"user.address.city\")\n- `default_val` (optional) - Value to return if path doesn't exist\n\n**Returns:** Value at path, or `default_val`, or null\n\n**Path syntax:**\n- `\"user.name\"` - Object property access\n- `\"items.0\"` - Array index access (numeric parts)\n- `\"\"` - Empty path returns root object\n\n---\n\n#### `set(obj, path: string, value)`\n\nSet value by path. Modifies object in-place.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { set } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet doc = { user: { name: \"Alice\" }, items: [1, 2, 3] };\n\n// Update nested property\nset(doc, \"user.name\", \"Bob\");\nprint(doc.user.name); // \"Bob\"\n\n// Update array element\nset(doc, \"items.1\", 99);\nprint(doc.items[1]); // 99\n\n// Add new property\nset(doc, \"user.email\", \"bob@example.com\");\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `obj` - Root object to modify\n- `path` (string) - Dot-separated path\n- `value` - New value to set\n\n**Returns:** null\n\n**Throws:** Error if path does not exist (intermediate nodes must exist)\n\n---\n\n#### `has(obj, path: string): bool`\n\nCheck if path exists in object.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { has } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet doc = { user: { name: \"Alice\", age: 30 } };\n\nprint(has(doc, \"user.name\")); // true\nprint(has(doc, \"user.email\")); // false\nprint(has(doc, \"items\")); // false\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `obj` - Root object\n- `path` (string) - Dot-separated path\n\n**Returns:** true if path exists, false otherwise\n\n---\n\n#### `delete(obj, path: string): bool`\n\nDelete a property by path. Supports both object properties and array elements.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { delete, has } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet doc = { user: { name: \"Alice\", email: \"alice@example.com\" } };\n\nprint(delete(doc, \"user.email\")); // true\nprint(has(doc, \"user.email\")); // false\n\n// Also works with array indices\nlet arr = { items: [1, 2, 3] };\ndelete(arr, \"items.1\"); // Removes element at index 1\n// arr.items is now [1, 3]\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `obj` - Root object\n- `path` (string) - Path to delete\n\n**Returns:** `true` if the property was deleted, `false` if not found\n\nSupports deleting both object properties and array elements (by index).\n\n---\n\n### Validation\n\n#### `is_valid(json_str: string): bool`\n\nCheck if string is valid JSON (lightweight check).\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_valid } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nprint(is_valid('{\"x\":10}')); // true\nprint(is_valid('{\"invalid}')); // false\nprint(is_valid('[1,2,3]')); // true\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `json_str` (string) - JSON string to validate\n\n**Returns:** true if valid, false otherwise\n\n**Note:** Parses the string to validate (not a regex check)\n\n---\n\n#### `validate(json_str: string)`\n\nValidate JSON and return detailed result object.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { validate } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet result = validate('{\"x\":10}');\nprint(result.valid); // true\n\nlet result2 = validate('{\"unclosed\"');\nprint(result2.valid); // false\nprint(result2.message); // Error message\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `json_str` (string) - JSON string to validate\n\n**Returns:** Object with fields:\n- `valid` (bool) - true if valid\n- `message` (string) - Error message or \"Valid JSON\"\n- `line` (i32) - Line number of error (-1 if not available)\n\n---\n\n### Type Checking\n\n#### `is_object(value): bool`\n\nCheck if value is an object.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_object } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nprint(is_object({})); // true\nprint(is_object({ x: 10 })); // true\nprint(is_object([])); // false\nprint(is_object(\"text\")); // false\n```\n\n---\n\n#### `is_array(value): bool`\n\nCheck if value is an array.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_array } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nprint(is_array([])); // true\nprint(is_array([1, 2, 3])); // true\nprint(is_array({})); // false\n```\n\n---\n\n#### `is_string(value): bool`, `is_number(value): bool`, `is_bool(value): bool`, `is_null(value): bool`\n\nCheck value types.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_string, is_number, is_bool, is_null } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nprint(is_string(\"hello\")); // true\nprint(is_number(42)); // true\nprint(is_number(3.14)); // true\nprint(is_bool(true)); // true\nprint(is_null(null)); // true\n```\n\n---\n\n#### `type_of(value): string`\n\nGet JSON type as string.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { type_of } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nprint(type_of({})); // \"object\"\nprint(type_of([])); // \"array\"\nprint(type_of(\"text\")); // \"string\"\nprint(type_of(42)); // \"number\"\nprint(type_of(true)); // \"bool\"\nprint(type_of(null)); // \"null\"\n```\n\n**Returns:** Type name: \"object\", \"array\", \"string\", \"number\", \"bool\", \"null\"\n\n---\n\n### Clone & Merge\n\n#### `clone(value)`\n\nCreate deep copy of value (independent copy).\n\n```hemlock\nimport { clone } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet original = { x: 10, items: [1, 2, 3] };\nlet copy = clone(original);\n\ncopy.x = 20;\ncopy.items.push(4);\n\nprint(original.x); // 10 (unchanged)\nprint(original.items.length); // 3 (unchanged)\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `value` - Value to clone\n\n**Returns:** Deep copy of value\n\n**Implementation:** Uses serialize/deserialize for reliable deep copy\n\n---\n\n#### `merge(base, update)`\n\nDeep merge objects (combines nested objects).\n\n```hemlock\nlet base = { x: 10, nested: { a: 1 } };\nlet update = { y: 20, nested: { b: 2 } };\nlet result = merge(base, update);\n// { x: 10, y: 20, nested: { a: 1, b: 2 } }\n```\n\n---\n\n#### `patch(base, update)`\n\nShallow merge (replaces nested objects).\n\n\n---\n\n### Comparison\n\n#### `equals(a, b): bool`\n\nDeep equality check for values.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { equals } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet obj1 = { x: 10, items: [1, 2, 3] };\nlet obj2 = { x: 10, items: [1, 2, 3] };\n\nprint(equals(obj1, obj2)); // true\n\nobj2.x = 20;\nprint(equals(obj1, obj2)); // false\n\n// Array comparison\nprint(equals([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3])); // true\nprint(equals([1, 2, 3], [1, 2])); // false\n```\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `a`, `b` - Values to compare\n\n**Returns:** true if deeply equal, false otherwise\n\n\n---\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Configuration Management\n\n```hemlock\nimport { parse_file, pretty_file, get, set } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\n// Load configuration\nlet config = parse_file(\"config.json\");\n\n// Read settings with defaults\nlet port = get(config, \"server.port\", 8080);\nlet host = get(config, \"server.host\", \"localhost\");\nlet db_pool = get(config, \"database.pool_size\", 10);\n\nprint(\"Server: \" + host + \":\" + typeof(port));\n\n// Update settings\nset(config, \"server.port\", 9000);\nset(config, \"database.pool_size\", 20);\n\n// Save with formatting\npretty_file(\"config.json\", config, 2);\n```\n\n### API Response Processing\n\n```hemlock\nimport { parse, get, is_array } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet response = parse(http_response_body);\n\n// Extract data safely\nlet users = get(response, \"data.users\", []);\n\nif (is_array(users)) {\n print(\"Found \" + typeof(users.length) + \" users\");\n\n let i = 0;\n while (i < users.length) {\n let name = get(users[i], \"name\", \"Unknown\");\n let email = get(users[i], \"email\", \"N/A\");\n print(name + \" <\" + email + \">\");\n i = i + 1;\n }\n}\n```\n\n### Data Transformation\n\n```hemlock\nimport { parse, stringify, clone } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nlet input = parse(input_json);\n\n// Clone to avoid mutating original\nlet output = clone(input);\n\n// Transform data\nset(output, \"metadata.processed\", true);\nset(output, \"metadata.timestamp\", time());\n\n// Output as JSON\nlet result_json = stringify(output);\n```\n\n### Validation Workflow\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_valid, validate, parse } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\nfn process_json_input(user_input: string) {\n // Quick validation\n if (!is_valid(user_input)) {\n let result = validate(user_input);\n print(\"Invalid JSON: \" + result.message);\n return null;\n }\n\n // Parse and process\n let data = parse(user_input);\n\n // Validate structure\n if (!has(data, \"version\")) {\n print(\"Missing required field: version\");\n return null;\n }\n\n return data;\n}\n```\n\n## Performance Notes\n\n### Fast Operations\n- `parse()` / `stringify()` - Built-in C implementation\n- `get()` / `set()` - Direct property/array access\n- `is_valid()` - Single parse attempt\n- Type checks - Simple typeof() calls\n\n### Slower Operations\n- `pretty()` - Recursive formatting with string concatenation\n- `clone()` - Serialize + deserialize round-trip\n- `equals()` - Deep recursive comparison\n\n### Memory Usage\n- `clone()` - Creates full independent copy (2x memory)\n- `pretty()` - Builds large string in memory\n- `parse()` - Allocates objects/arrays on heap\n\n## Error Handling\n\nAll JSON operations use Hemlock's exception system:\n\n```hemlock\nimport { parse, stringify, get, set } from \"@stdlib/json\";\n\n// Parse errors\ntry {\n let obj = parse('{\"malformed}');\n} catch (e) {\n print(\"Parse error: \" + e);\n}\n\n// Serialization errors (circular references)\ntry {\n let obj = {};\n obj.self = obj;\n stringify(obj);\n} catch (e) {\n print(\"Stringify error: \" + e);\n}\n\n// Path errors\ntry {\n let obj = { user: { name: \"Alice\" } };\n set(obj, \"nonexistent.path\", \"value\");\n} catch (e) {\n print(\"Path error: \" + e);\n}\n```\n\n## Current Limitations\n\n1. **No line numbers in parse errors** - Validation doesn't report exact error location\n3. **No JSON Schema** - Schema validation not yet supported\n4. **No streaming** - Large files must fit in memory\n\n## Future Enhancements\n\nPlanned additions:\n- JSON Schema validation\n- JSON Patch (RFC 6902)\n- JSON Pointer (RFC 6901)\n- Streaming parser for large files\n- JSON5 support (comments, trailing commas)\n\n## See Also\n\n- Built-in `serialize()` method (CLAUDE.md - Objects section)\n- Built-in `deserialize()` method (CLAUDE.md - Strings section)\n- `@stdlib/fs` - File operations\n- `@stdlib/http` - HTTP requests with JSON\n"}, "Bibliothèque standard -> logging": {"id": "stdlib-logging", "content": "# @stdlib/logging - Logging Module\n\nComprehensive logging facilities for Hemlock applications with support for log levels, structured logging, file output, and filtering.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Overview](#stdlib-logging/overview)\n- [Log Levels](#stdlib-logging/log-levels)\n- [Logger Factory](#stdlib-logging/logger-factory)\n- [Logging Methods](#stdlib-logging/logging-methods)\n- [Configuration](#stdlib-logging/configuration)\n- [Structured Logging](#stdlib-logging/structured-logging)\n- [Default Logger](#stdlib-logging/default-logger)\n- [Examples](#stdlib-logging/examples)\n- [Best Practices](#stdlib-logging/best-practices)\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\nThe logging module provides a flexible and powerful logging system for Hemlock applications. It supports:\n\n- **Four log levels** (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR)\n- **Structured logging** with key-value pairs (JSON)\n- **Output to stdout or file**\n- **Configurable formatting**\n- **Log level filtering**\n- **Timestamps** (Unix epoch format)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\nlet logger = Logger({ level: INFO, output: \"app.log\" });\nlogger.info(\"Application started\");\nlogger.warn(\"Low memory warning\");\nlogger.error(\"Database connection failed\");\n```\n\n---\n\n## Log Levels\n\nThe module provides four standard log levels as constants:\n\n### Constants\n\n- **`DEBUG = 0`** - Detailed diagnostic information\n- **`INFO = 1`** - General informational messages\n- **`WARN = 2`** - Warning messages (potential issues)\n- **`ERROR = 3`** - Error messages (serious problems)\n\n### Level Hierarchy\n\nLog levels form a hierarchy where higher levels are more severe:\n\n```\nDEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR\n 0 1 2 3\n```\n\nWhen you set a minimum log level, messages below that level are filtered out.\n\n**Example:**\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\nlet logger = Logger({ level: WARN }); // Only WARN and ERROR\n\nlogger.debug(\"This is filtered\"); // Not shown\nlogger.info(\"This is filtered\"); // Not shown\nlogger.warn(\"This is shown\"); // ✓ Shown\nlogger.error(\"This is shown\"); // ✓ Shown\n```\n\n---\n\n## Logger Factory\n\n### `Logger(config?)`\n\nCreate a logger instance with optional configuration.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `config` (object, optional) - Configuration options\n\n**Configuration Options:**\n\n| Option | Type | Default | Description |\n|--------|------|---------|-------------|\n| `output` | string | `\"stdout\"` | Output target: `\"stdout\"` or file path |\n| `level` | i32 | `INFO` | Minimum log level to output |\n| `format` | string | `\"{timestamp} [{level}] {message}\"` | Log message format |\n| `include_timestamp` | bool | `true` | Whether to include timestamps |\n\n**Returns:** Logger object\n\n**Format String Placeholders:**\n- `{timestamp}` - Unix timestamp\n- `{level}` - Log level name (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR)\n- `{message}` - Log message content\n\n**Example:**\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger, DEBUG } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\n// Basic logger (stdout, INFO level)\nlet logger1 = Logger();\n\n// Custom configuration\nlet logger2 = Logger({\n output: \"/var/log/app.log\",\n level: DEBUG,\n format: \"[{level}] {message}\",\n include_timestamp: false\n});\n\n// Don't forget to close file loggers!\ndefer logger2.close();\n```\n\n---\n\n## Logging Methods\n\nLogger objects provide five methods for logging messages:\n\n### `logger.debug(message, data?)`\n\nLog a DEBUG level message.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `message` (any) - Message to log (automatically converted to string)\n- `data` (object, optional) - Structured data (key-value pairs)\n\n**Returns:** null\n\n**Example:**\n```hemlock\nlogger.debug(\"Variable value\", { x: 42, y: 100 });\n```\n\n---\n\n### `logger.info(message, data?)`\n\nLog an INFO level message.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `message` (any) - Message to log\n- `data` (object, optional) - Structured data\n\n**Returns:** null\n\n**Example:**\n```hemlock\nlogger.info(\"Server started\", { port: 8080, pid: 12345 });\n```\n\n---\n\n### `logger.warn(message, data?)`\n\nLog a WARN level message.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `message` (any) - Message to log\n- `data` (object, optional) - Structured data\n\n**Returns:** null\n\n**Example:**\n```hemlock\nlogger.warn(\"High CPU usage\", { cpu: 95.5, threshold: 80.0 });\n```\n\n---\n\n### `logger.error(message, data?)`\n\nLog an ERROR level message.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `message` (any) - Message to log\n- `data` (object, optional) - Structured data\n\n**Returns:** null\n\n**Example:**\n```hemlock\nlogger.error(\"Database error\", { code: 500, message: \"Connection timeout\" });\n```\n\n---\n\n### `logger.log(level, message, data?)`\n\nLog a message with an explicit log level.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `level` (i32) - Log level constant (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR)\n- `message` (any) - Message to log\n- `data` (object, optional) - Structured data\n\n**Returns:** null\n\n**Example:**\n```hemlock\nimport { DEBUG } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\nlet severity = DEBUG;\nlogger.log(severity, \"Custom level logging\");\n```\n\n---\n\n## Configuration\n\n### `logger.set_level(level)`\n\nChange the minimum log level dynamically.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `level` (i32) - New minimum log level\n\n**Returns:** null\n\n**Example:**\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger, DEBUG, INFO, ERROR } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\nlet logger = Logger({ level: INFO });\n\nlogger.debug(\"Not shown\"); // Filtered\nlogger.info(\"Shown\"); // ✓\n\n// Change to DEBUG level\nlogger.set_level(DEBUG);\n\nlogger.debug(\"Now shown\"); // ✓\nlogger.info(\"Still shown\"); // ✓\n\n// Change to ERROR only\nlogger.set_level(ERROR);\n\nlogger.info(\"Not shown\"); // Filtered\nlogger.warn(\"Not shown\"); // Filtered\nlogger.error(\"Shown\"); // ✓\n```\n\n---\n\n### `logger.close()`\n\nClose the file handle if using file output. Safe to call multiple times.\n\n**Returns:** null\n\n**Example:**\n```hemlock\nlet logger = Logger({ output: \"app.log\" });\n\n// ... use logger ...\n\nlogger.close(); // Close file when done\n```\n\n**Best Practice:** Always close file loggers to prevent resource leaks:\n\n```hemlock\nlet logger = Logger({ output: \"app.log\" });\ndefer logger.close(); // Automatic cleanup\n\n// ... use logger ...\n```\n\n---\n\n## Structured Logging\n\nStructured logging allows you to attach machine-readable key-value data to log messages.\n\n### Basic Structured Logging\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger, INFO } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\nlet logger = Logger();\n\n// Log with structured data\nlogger.info(\"User login\", {\n user_id: 12345,\n username: \"alice\",\n ip_address: \"192.168.1.100\",\n timestamp: 1638360000\n});\n\n// Output: 1638360123 [INFO] User login {\"user_id\":12345,\"username\":\"alice\",\"ip_address\":\"192.168.1.100\",\"timestamp\":1638360000}\n```\n\n### Nested Objects\n\n```hemlock\nlogger.error(\"API request failed\", {\n endpoint: \"/api/users\",\n status: 500,\n error: {\n code: \"TIMEOUT\",\n message: \"Request timed out after 30s\",\n retry_count: 3\n }\n});\n\n// Output includes nested JSON\n```\n\n### Arrays in Structured Data\n\n```hemlock\nlogger.warn(\"Multiple validation errors\", {\n field: \"email\",\n errors: [\"Invalid format\", \"Domain not allowed\", \"Too long\"]\n});\n```\n\n---\n\n## Default Logger\n\nThe module provides a default logger instance and convenience functions for quick logging:\n\n### Default Logger Instance\n\n```hemlock\nimport { default_logger } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\ndefault_logger.info(\"Quick log message\");\n```\n\n### Convenience Functions\n\n```hemlock\nimport { debug, info, warn, error, log } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\nimport { DEBUG } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\n// These use the default logger internally\ndebug(\"Debug message\");\ninfo(\"Info message\");\nwarn(\"Warning message\");\nerror(\"Error message\");\nlog(DEBUG, \"Custom level\");\n\n// With structured data\ninfo(\"User action\", { action: \"click\", button: \"submit\" });\n```\n\n**Note:** The default logger outputs to stdout with INFO level.\n\n---\n\n## Examples\n\n### Example 1: Basic Console Logging\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger, INFO } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\nlet logger = Logger();\n\nlogger.info(\"Application starting...\");\nlogger.info(\"Loading configuration\");\nlogger.info(\"Server ready on port 8080\");\n```\n\n**Output:**\n```\n1638360123 [INFO] Application starting...\n1638360124 [INFO] Loading configuration\n1638360125 [INFO] Server ready on port 8080\n```\n\n---\n\n### Example 2: File Logging with Error Handling\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger, ERROR } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\nlet logger = Logger({\n output: \"/var/log/myapp.log\",\n level: ERROR\n});\ndefer logger.close();\n\ntry {\n risky_operation();\n} catch (e) {\n logger.error(\"Operation failed\", {\n error: e,\n timestamp: __now(),\n context: \"main_loop\"\n });\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### Example 3: Debug Logging During Development\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger, DEBUG } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\nlet logger = Logger({ level: DEBUG });\n\nfn process_data(data: array) {\n logger.debug(\"Processing started\", { size: data.length });\n\n let i = 0;\n while (i < data.length) {\n logger.debug(\"Processing item\", { index: i, value: data[i] });\n // ... process item ...\n i = i + 1;\n }\n\n logger.debug(\"Processing completed\");\n return null;\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### Example 4: Dynamic Log Level\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger, DEBUG, INFO, getenv } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\nimport { getenv } from \"@stdlib/env\";\n\n// Set log level from environment variable\nlet log_level = INFO;\nlet env_level = getenv(\"LOG_LEVEL\");\n\nif (env_level == \"DEBUG\") {\n log_level = DEBUG;\n}\n\nlet logger = Logger({ level: log_level });\n\nlogger.debug(\"This shows only if LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG\");\nlogger.info(\"This always shows\");\n```\n\n---\n\n### Example 5: HTTP Request Logging\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\nlet access_log = Logger({\n output: \"access.log\",\n format: \"{timestamp} {message}\"\n});\ndefer access_log.close();\n\nfn handle_request(request) {\n let start = __time_ms();\n\n // ... handle request ...\n\n let elapsed = __time_ms() - start;\n\n access_log.info(\"HTTP request\", {\n method: request.method,\n path: request.path,\n status: 200,\n duration_ms: elapsed,\n ip: request.client_ip\n });\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### Example 6: Multiple Loggers\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger, DEBUG, ERROR } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\n// Application logger (stdout, all levels)\nlet app_logger = Logger({ level: DEBUG });\n\n// Error logger (file, errors only)\nlet error_logger = Logger({\n output: \"errors.log\",\n level: ERROR\n});\ndefer error_logger.close();\n\nfn process() {\n app_logger.debug(\"Starting process\");\n\n try {\n // ... work ...\n app_logger.info(\"Process completed\");\n } catch (e) {\n app_logger.error(\"Process failed\");\n error_logger.error(\"Critical error\", {\n error: e,\n timestamp: __now()\n });\n }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### Example 7: Custom Format\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Logger } from \"@stdlib/logging\";\n\nlet logger = Logger({\n format: \"[{level}] {message}\",\n include_timestamp: false\n});\n\nlogger.info(\"Clean output without timestamp\");\n// Output: [INFO] Clean output without timestamp\n\nlet logger2 = Logger({\n format: \"{level}: {message}\"\n});\n\nlogger2.warn(\"Custom separator\");\n// Output: WARN: Custom separator\n```\n\n---\n\n## Best Practices\n\n### 1. Always Close File Loggers\n\nUse `defer` to ensure cleanup:\n\n```hemlock\nlet logger = Logger({ output: \"app.log\" });\ndefer logger.close();\n```\n\n### 2. Use Appropriate Log Levels\n\n- **DEBUG**: Verbose diagnostic info (disabled in production)\n- **INFO**: Normal application events\n- **WARN**: Potentially harmful situations\n- **ERROR**: Error events that might still allow the app to continue\n\n### 3. Include Context with Structured Data\n\n```hemlock\n// Good: Provides context\nlogger.error(\"Database query failed\", {\n query: \"SELECT * FROM users\",\n duration_ms: 5000,\n error: \"Timeout\"\n});\n\n// Less useful: No context\nlogger.error(\"Query failed\");\n```\n\n### 4. Configure from Environment\n\n```hemlock\nimport { getenv } from \"@stdlib/env\";\n\nlet log_level = INFO;\nlet env_level = getenv(\"LOG_LEVEL\");\nif (env_level == \"DEBUG\") {\n log_level = DEBUG;\n}\n\nlet logger = Logger({ level: log_level });\n```\n\n### 5. Separate Concerns with Multiple Loggers\n\n```hemlock\nlet app_logger = Logger({ output: \"app.log\" });\nlet access_logger = Logger({ output: \"access.log\" });\nlet error_logger = Logger({ output: \"error.log\", level: ERROR });\n\ndefer app_logger.close();\ndefer access_logger.close();\ndefer error_logger.close();\n```\n\n### 6. Avoid Logging Sensitive Data\n\n```hemlock\n// Bad: Logs password\nlogger.info(\"User login\", { username: \"alice\", password: \"secret123\" });\n\n// Good: Omit sensitive data\nlogger.info(\"User login\", { username: \"alice\" });\n```\n\n---\n\n## Implementation Details\n\n### Format String Processing\n\nThe format string uses simple `replace()` operations for placeholder substitution. Custom format strings can use any combination of:\n- `{timestamp}` - Unix epoch timestamp\n- `{level}` - Log level name\n- `{message}` - Log message\n\n### Timestamp Format\n\nTimestamps are currently Unix epoch seconds (i64). Future versions may support ISO 8601 formatting.\n\n### Structured Data Serialization\n\nStructured data is serialized to JSON using the object's `.serialize()` method. Circular references will throw an error.\n\n### File Handling\n\n- Files are opened in append mode (`\"a\"`)\n- If file open fails, logger falls back to stdout\n- File handles must be explicitly closed with `logger.close()`\n\n---\n\n## Future Enhancements\n\nPlanned improvements:\n- ISO 8601 timestamp formatting\n- Log rotation (size-based and time-based)\n- Async logging (non-blocking file writes)\n- Log compression\n- Remote logging (syslog, HTTP endpoints)\n- Log parsing utilities\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- [@stdlib/time](#stdlib-time) - Time functions used for timestamps\n- [@stdlib/fs](#stdlib-fs) - File operations used for file logging\n"}, "Bibliothèque standard -> math": {"id": "stdlib-math", "content": "# Hemlock Math Module\n\nA standard library module providing mathematical functions and constants for Hemlock programs.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe math module provides comprehensive mathematical operations including:\n\n- **Trigonometric functions** - sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2\n- **Exponential & logarithmic functions** - sqrt, pow, exp, log, log10, log2\n- **Rounding functions** - floor, ceil, round, trunc\n- **Sign & special functions** - sign, cbrt, hypot, gcd, lcm\n- **Hyperbolic functions** - sinh, cosh, tanh\n- **Utility functions** - abs, min, max, clamp\n- **Random number generation** - rand, rand_range, seed\n- **Mathematical constants** - PI, E, TAU, INF, NAN\n\n## Usage\n\n```hemlock\nimport { sin, cos, PI } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet angle = PI / 4;\nlet x = cos(angle);\nlet y = sin(angle);\n```\n\nOr import all:\n\n```hemlock\nimport * as math from \"@stdlib/math\";\nlet result = math.sqrt(16);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Constants\n\n### PI\nThe mathematical constant π (pi) ≈ 3.14159265358979323846\n\n```hemlock\nimport { PI } from \"@stdlib/math\";\nlet circumference = 2.0 * PI * radius;\n```\n\n### E\nThe mathematical constant e (Euler's number) ≈ 2.71828182845904523536\n\n```hemlock\nimport { E } from \"@stdlib/math\";\nlet growth = E * rate;\n```\n\n### TAU\nThe mathematical constant τ (tau) = 2π ≈ 6.28318530717958647692\n\n```hemlock\nimport { TAU } from \"@stdlib/math\";\nlet full_circle = TAU; // One complete rotation in radians\n```\n\n### INF\nPositive infinity (IEEE 754 floating point infinity)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { INF } from \"@stdlib/math\";\nlet max_value = INF;\n```\n\n### NAN\nNot-a-Number (IEEE 754 floating point NaN)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { NAN } from \"@stdlib/math\";\nlet undefined_result = NAN;\n```\n\n---\n\n## Trigonometric Functions\n\nAll trigonometric functions work with radians.\n\n### sin(x)\nReturns the sine of x (x in radians).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Angle in radians\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Sine of x in range [-1, 1]\n\n```hemlock\nimport { sin, PI } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = sin(0.0); // 0.0\nlet result2 = sin(PI / 2.0); // 1.0\nlet result3 = sin(PI); // ~0.0\n```\n\n### cos(x)\nReturns the cosine of x (x in radians).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Angle in radians\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Cosine of x in range [-1, 1]\n\n```hemlock\nimport { cos, PI } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = cos(0.0); // 1.0\nlet result2 = cos(PI / 2.0); // ~0.0\nlet result3 = cos(PI); // -1.0\n```\n\n### tan(x)\nReturns the tangent of x (x in radians).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Angle in radians\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Tangent of x\n\n```hemlock\nimport { tan, PI } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = tan(0.0); // 0.0\nlet result2 = tan(PI / 4.0); // 1.0\n```\n\n### asin(x)\nReturns the arc sine (inverse sine) of x in radians.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Value in range [-1, 1]\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Arc sine in range [-π/2, π/2]\n\n```hemlock\nimport { asin, PI } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet angle = asin(1.0); // π/2\nlet angle2 = asin(0.5); // π/6\n```\n\n### acos(x)\nReturns the arc cosine (inverse cosine) of x in radians.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Value in range [-1, 1]\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Arc cosine in range [0, π]\n\n```hemlock\nimport { acos, PI } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet angle = acos(0.0); // π/2\nlet angle2 = acos(1.0); // 0.0\n```\n\n### atan(x)\nReturns the arc tangent (inverse tangent) of x in radians.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any real number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Arc tangent in range [-π/2, π/2]\n\n```hemlock\nimport { atan } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet angle = atan(1.0); // π/4\nlet angle2 = atan(0.0); // 0.0\n```\n\n### atan2(y, x)\nReturns the arc tangent of y/x in radians, using the signs of both arguments to determine the quadrant.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `y: number` - Y coordinate\n- `x: number` - X coordinate\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Arc tangent in range [-π, π]\n\n```hemlock\nimport { atan2, PI } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet angle = atan2(1.0, 1.0); // π/4 (45 degrees)\nlet angle2 = atan2(1.0, -1.0); // 3π/4 (135 degrees)\nlet angle3 = atan2(-1.0, -1.0); // -3π/4 (-135 degrees)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Exponential & Logarithmic Functions\n\n### sqrt(x)\nReturns the square root of x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Non-negative number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Square root of x\n\n```hemlock\nimport { sqrt } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = sqrt(16.0); // 4.0\nlet result2 = sqrt(2.0); // 1.414213...\nlet result3 = sqrt(0.0); // 0.0\n```\n\n### pow(base, exponent)\nReturns base raised to the power of exponent.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `base: number` - Base value\n- `exponent: number` - Exponent value\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - base^exponent\n\n```hemlock\nimport { pow } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = pow(2.0, 3.0); // 8.0\nlet result2 = pow(10.0, 2.0); // 100.0\nlet result3 = pow(4.0, 0.5); // 2.0 (square root)\n```\n\n### exp(x)\nReturns e raised to the power of x (e^x).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Exponent\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - e^x\n\n```hemlock\nimport { exp } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = exp(0.0); // 1.0\nlet result2 = exp(1.0); // 2.718281... (e)\nlet result3 = exp(2.0); // 7.389056...\n```\n\n### log(x)\nReturns the natural logarithm (base e) of x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Positive number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - ln(x)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { log, E } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = log(1.0); // 0.0\nlet result2 = log(E); // 1.0\nlet result3 = log(10.0); // 2.302585...\n```\n\n### log10(x)\nReturns the base-10 logarithm of x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Positive number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - log₁₀(x)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { log10 } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = log10(1.0); // 0.0\nlet result2 = log10(10.0); // 1.0\nlet result3 = log10(100.0); // 2.0\n```\n\n### log2(x)\nReturns the base-2 logarithm of x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Positive number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - log₂(x)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { log2 } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = log2(1.0); // 0.0\nlet result2 = log2(2.0); // 1.0\nlet result3 = log2(8.0); // 3.0\n```\n\n---\n\n## Rounding Functions\n\n### floor(x)\nReturns the largest integer less than or equal to x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Floor of x\n\n```hemlock\nimport { floor } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = floor(3.7); // 3.0\nlet result2 = floor(-2.3); // -3.0\nlet result3 = floor(5.0); // 5.0\n```\n\n### ceil(x)\nReturns the smallest integer greater than or equal to x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Ceiling of x\n\n```hemlock\nimport { ceil } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = ceil(3.2); // 4.0\nlet result2 = ceil(-2.7); // -2.0\nlet result3 = ceil(5.0); // 5.0\n```\n\n### round(x)\nReturns x rounded to the nearest integer. Halfway cases round away from zero.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Rounded value\n\n```hemlock\nimport { round } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = round(3.5); // 4.0\nlet result2 = round(3.4); // 3.0\nlet result3 = round(-2.5); // -3.0\n```\n\n### trunc(x)\nReturns the integer part of x, removing any fractional digits (rounds toward zero).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Truncated value\n\n```hemlock\nimport { trunc } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = trunc(3.7); // 3.0\nlet result2 = trunc(-2.9); // -2.0\nlet result3 = trunc(5.0); // 5.0\n```\n\n---\n\n## Division Functions\n\n### div(a, b)\nReturns the floating-point division of a by b. Equivalent to the `/` operator.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `a: number` - Dividend\n- `b: number` - Divisor\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Floating-point result\n\n```hemlock\nimport { div } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = div(7, 2); // 3.5\n```\n\n### divi(a, b)\nReturns the integer division of a by b (truncates toward zero).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `a: number` - Dividend\n- `b: number` - Divisor\n\n**Returns:** `i32` or `i64` - Integer result (truncated toward zero)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { divi } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = divi(7, 2); // 3\nlet result2 = divi(-7, 2); // -3\n```\n\n### floori(x)\nReturns the floor of x as an integer (rounds toward negative infinity).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `i32` or `i64` - Integer floor\n\n```hemlock\nimport { floori } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = floori(3.7); // 3\nlet result2 = floori(-2.3); // -3\n```\n\n### ceili(x)\nReturns the ceiling of x as an integer (rounds toward positive infinity).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `i32` or `i64` - Integer ceiling\n\n```hemlock\nimport { ceili } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = ceili(3.2); // 4\nlet result2 = ceili(-2.7); // -2\n```\n\n### roundi(x)\nReturns x rounded to the nearest integer. Halfway cases round away from zero.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `i32` or `i64` - Rounded integer\n\n```hemlock\nimport { roundi } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = roundi(3.5); // 4\nlet result2 = roundi(3.4); // 3\nlet result3 = roundi(-2.5); // -3\n```\n\n### trunci(x)\nReturns the integer part of x (truncates toward zero). Same as `divi(x, 1)`.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `i32` or `i64` - Truncated integer\n\n```hemlock\nimport { trunci } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = trunci(3.7); // 3\nlet result2 = trunci(-2.9); // -2\n```\n\n---\n\n## Sign & Special Functions\n\n### sign(x)\nReturns -1, 0, or 1 based on the sign of x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `i32` - -1 if negative, 0 if zero, 1 if positive\n\n```hemlock\nimport { sign } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = sign(-5.0); // -1\nlet result2 = sign(0.0); // 0\nlet result3 = sign(3.2); // 1\n```\n\n### cbrt(x)\nReturns the cube root of x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Cube root of x\n\n```hemlock\nimport { cbrt } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = cbrt(27.0); // 3.0\nlet result2 = cbrt(-8.0); // -2.0\nlet result3 = cbrt(0.0); // 0.0\n```\n\n### hypot(x, y)\nReturns the hypotenuse: sqrt(x^2 + y^2).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - First value\n- `y: number` - Second value\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - sqrt(x^2 + y^2)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { hypot } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = hypot(3.0, 4.0); // 5.0\n```\n\n### gcd(a, b)\nReturns the greatest common divisor of a and b.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `a: number` - First value\n- `b: number` - Second value\n\n**Returns:** `i64` - Greatest common divisor\n\n```hemlock\nimport { gcd } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = gcd(12, 8); // 4\nlet result2 = gcd(54, 24); // 6\n```\n\n### lcm(a, b)\nReturns the least common multiple of a and b.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `a: number` - First value\n- `b: number` - Second value\n\n**Returns:** `i64` - Least common multiple\n\n```hemlock\nimport { lcm } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = lcm(4, 6); // 12\nlet result2 = lcm(3, 7); // 21\n```\n\n---\n\n## Hyperbolic Functions\n\n### sinh(x)\nReturns the hyperbolic sine of x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Hyperbolic sine of x\n\n```hemlock\nimport { sinh } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = sinh(0.0); // 0.0\nlet result2 = sinh(1.0); // 1.175201...\n```\n\n### cosh(x)\nReturns the hyperbolic cosine of x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Hyperbolic cosine of x\n\n```hemlock\nimport { cosh } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = cosh(0.0); // 1.0\nlet result2 = cosh(1.0); // 1.543080...\n```\n\n### tanh(x)\nReturns the hyperbolic tangent of x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Hyperbolic tangent of x in range (-1, 1)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { tanh } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = tanh(0.0); // 0.0\nlet result2 = tanh(1.0); // 0.761594...\n```\n\n---\n\n## Utility Functions\n\n### abs(x)\nReturns the absolute value of x.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `x: number` - Any number\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - |x|\n\n```hemlock\nimport { abs } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = abs(-5.0); // 5.0\nlet result2 = abs(3.2); // 3.2\nlet result3 = abs(0.0); // 0.0\n```\n\n### min(a, b)\nReturns the smaller of two values.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `a: number` - First value\n- `b: number` - Second value\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Minimum of a and b\n\n```hemlock\nimport { min } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = min(5.0, 10.0); // 5.0\nlet result2 = min(-3.0, 2.0); // -3.0\n```\n\n### max(a, b)\nReturns the larger of two values.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `a: number` - First value\n- `b: number` - Second value\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Maximum of a and b\n\n```hemlock\nimport { max } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = max(5.0, 10.0); // 10.0\nlet result2 = max(-3.0, 2.0); // 2.0\n```\n\n### clamp(value, min_val, max_val)\nConstrains a value to lie within a range [min, max].\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `value: number` - Value to clamp\n- `min_val: number` - Minimum bound\n- `max_val: number` - Maximum bound\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Clamped value\n\n```hemlock\nimport { clamp } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result = clamp(5.0, 0.0, 10.0); // 5.0\nlet result2 = clamp(-3.0, 0.0, 10.0); // 0.0 (clamped to min)\nlet result3 = clamp(15.0, 0.0, 10.0); // 10.0 (clamped to max)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Random Number Generation\n\n### rand()\nReturns a random floating-point number in the range [0.0, 1.0).\n\n**Parameters:** None\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Random value in [0.0, 1.0)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { rand } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet random = rand(); // e.g., 0.7382491...\nlet random2 = rand(); // e.g., 0.2194837...\n```\n\n### rand_range(min_val, max_val)\nReturns a random floating-point number in the range [min, max).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `min_val: number` - Minimum value (inclusive)\n- `max_val: number` - Maximum value (exclusive)\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Random value in [min, max)\n\n```hemlock\nimport { rand_range } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet dice = rand_range(1.0, 7.0); // Random 1.0 to 6.999...\nlet temperature = rand_range(20.0, 30.0); // Random 20-30°C\n```\n\n### seed(value)\nSeeds the random number generator with a specific value for reproducible sequences.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `value: i32` - Seed value\n\n**Returns:** `null`\n\n```hemlock\nimport { seed, rand } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nseed(42);\nlet r1 = rand(); // Same sequence every time with seed 42\nlet r2 = rand();\n\nseed(42); // Reset to same seed\nlet r3 = rand(); // r3 == r1\n```\n\n---\n\n## Complete Example\n\n```hemlock\nimport {\n sin, cos, tan, sqrt, pow,\n PI, abs, min, max,\n rand_range, seed\n} from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\n// Trigonometry: Calculate point on unit circle\nfn point_on_circle(angle: f64): object {\n return {\n x: cos(angle),\n y: sin(angle)\n };\n}\n\nlet p = point_on_circle(PI / 4.0);\nprint(\"Point at 45°: (\" + typeof(p.x) + \", \" + typeof(p.y) + \")\");\n\n// Distance formula\nfn distance(x1: f64, y1: f64, x2: f64, y2: f64): f64 {\n let dx = x2 - x1;\n let dy = y2 - y1;\n return sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);\n}\n\nlet dist = distance(0.0, 0.0, 3.0, 4.0);\nprint(\"Distance: \" + typeof(dist)); // 5.0\n\n// Random dice roller\nfn roll_dice(sides: i32): i32 {\n let result: i32 = rand_range(1.0, sides + 1.0);\n return result;\n}\n\nseed(42); // Reproducible results\nlet roll = roll_dice(6);\nprint(\"Dice roll: \" + typeof(roll));\n\n// Find max of three values\nfn max3(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64): f64 {\n return max(max(a, b), c);\n}\n\nprint(\"Max: \" + typeof(max3(5.0, 12.0, 8.0))); // 12.0\n```\n\n---\n\n## Implementation Notes\n\n- All functions wrap C standard library `` functions\n- All functions return `f64` (64-bit floating point)\n- Trigonometric functions use **radians**, not degrees\n- To convert degrees to radians: `radians = degrees * PI / 180.0`\n- To convert radians to degrees: `degrees = radians * 180.0 / PI`\n- Random number generator uses C `rand()` (not cryptographically secure)\n- `seed()` uses C `srand()` for seeding\n\n---\n\n## Error Handling\n\nMath functions follow C standard behavior:\n- `sqrt(-1.0)` returns `NAN`\n- `log(0.0)` returns `-INF`\n- `log(-1.0)` returns `NAN`\n- Division by zero in calculations returns `INF` or `NAN`\n- No exceptions are thrown for domain errors\n\n```hemlock\nimport { sqrt, log, NAN, INF } from \"@stdlib/math\";\n\nlet result1 = sqrt(-1.0); // NAN\nlet result2 = log(0.0); // -INF\nlet result3 = log(-1.0); // NAN\n\n// Check for invalid results\nif (result1 != result1) { // NAN != NAN is true\n print(\"Result is NaN\");\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\nRun the math module tests:\n\n```bash\n# Run all math tests\nmake test | grep stdlib_math\n\n# Or run individual test\n./hemlock tests/stdlib_math/test_math_constants.hml\n```\n\n---\n\n## License\n\nPart of the Hemlock standard library.\n"}, "Bibliothèque standard -> matrix": {"id": "stdlib-matrix", "content": "# Hemlock Matrix Module\n\nA standard library module providing dense matrix operations for linear algebra and numeric computation.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe matrix module provides:\n\n- **Matrix creation** - Constructor, identity, zeros, ones, diagonal, from arrays\n- **Element access** - get, set, row, col extraction\n- **Arithmetic** - add, sub, mul, scale, negate, hadamard\n- **Linear algebra** - det, inverse, solve, trace, norm, dot\n- **Utilities** - transpose, clone, submatrix, map, equals, to_string\n\n## Usage\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Matrix, identity, from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = Matrix(2, 3);\nm.set(0, 0, 1.0);\nm.set(0, 1, 2.0);\nprint(m.get(0, 1)); // 2.0\n```\n\nOr import all:\n\n```hemlock\nimport * as matrix from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\nlet I = matrix.identity(3);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Matrix Constructor\n\n### Matrix(rows, cols)\n\nCreates a new matrix initialized to zero.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `rows: i32` - Number of rows (must be positive)\n- `cols: i32` - Number of columns (must be positive)\n\n**Returns:** Matrix object\n\n**Throws:** If rows or cols are not positive\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Matrix } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = Matrix(3, 4); // 3x4 zero matrix\nm.set(0, 0, 5.0);\nprint(m.get(0, 0)); // 5.0\nprint(m.rows); // 3\nprint(m.cols); // 4\n```\n\n---\n\n## Factory Functions\n\n### from_array(rows, cols, values)\n\nCreates a matrix from a flat array in row-major order.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `rows: i32` - Number of rows\n- `cols: i32` - Number of columns\n- `values: array` - Flat array of values (length must equal rows * cols)\n\n**Returns:** Matrix object\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_array } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = from_array(2, 3, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);\n// [[1, 2, 3]\n// [4, 5, 6]]\n```\n\n### from_rows(row_arrays)\n\nCreates a matrix from an array of row arrays.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `row_arrays: array` - Array of arrays, each representing a row\n\n**Returns:** Matrix object\n\n**Throws:** If rows have different lengths or input is empty\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = from_rows([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]);\nprint(m.get(1, 2)); // 6\n```\n\n### identity(n)\n\nCreates an NxN identity matrix.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `n: i32` - Size of the matrix\n\n**Returns:** Matrix object with 1s on the diagonal, 0s elsewhere\n\n```hemlock\nimport { identity } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet I = identity(3);\n// [[1, 0, 0]\n// [0, 1, 0]\n// [0, 0, 1]]\n```\n\n### zeros(rows, cols)\n\nCreates a matrix filled with zeros.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `rows: i32` - Number of rows\n- `cols: i32` - Number of columns\n\n**Returns:** Matrix object\n\n```hemlock\nimport { zeros } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet z = zeros(2, 3); // 2x3 zero matrix\n```\n\n### ones(rows, cols)\n\nCreates a matrix filled with ones.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `rows: i32` - Number of rows\n- `cols: i32` - Number of columns\n\n**Returns:** Matrix object\n\n```hemlock\nimport { ones } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = ones(2, 2);\nprint(m.get(0, 0)); // 1.0\n```\n\n### diagonal(values)\n\nCreates a diagonal matrix from an array of values.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `values: array` - Values to place on the diagonal\n\n**Returns:** NxN Matrix object where N is the array length\n\n```hemlock\nimport { diagonal } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet d = diagonal([2, 3, 4]);\n// [[2, 0, 0]\n// [0, 3, 0]\n// [0, 0, 4]]\n```\n\n### col_vector(values)\n\nCreates an Nx1 column vector from an array.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `values: array` - Vector elements\n\n**Returns:** Nx1 Matrix object\n\n```hemlock\nimport { col_vector } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet v = col_vector([1, 2, 3]);\nprint(v.rows); // 3\nprint(v.cols); // 1\n```\n\n### row_vector(values)\n\nCreates a 1xN row vector from an array.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `values: array` - Vector elements\n\n**Returns:** 1xN Matrix object\n\n```hemlock\nimport { row_vector } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet v = row_vector([1, 2, 3]);\nprint(v.rows); // 1\nprint(v.cols); // 3\n```\n\n---\n\n## Matrix Methods\n\n### get(r, c)\n\nGets the element at row r, column c.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `r: i32` - Row index (0-based)\n- `c: i32` - Column index (0-based)\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Element value\n\n**Throws:** If indices are out of bounds\n\n### set(r, c, val)\n\nSets the element at row r, column c.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `r: i32` - Row index (0-based)\n- `c: i32` - Column index (0-based)\n- `val: f64` - Value to set\n\n**Throws:** If indices are out of bounds\n\n### row(r)\n\nReturns a row as an array.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `r: i32` - Row index\n\n**Returns:** `array` - Copy of the row\n\n### col(c)\n\nReturns a column as an array.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `c: i32` - Column index\n\n**Returns:** `array` - Copy of the column\n\n### to_array()\n\nReturns a flat copy of all elements in row-major order.\n\n**Returns:** `array` - Flat array of all elements\n\n### clone()\n\nReturns a deep copy of the matrix.\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix with identical dimensions and values\n\n---\n\n## Arithmetic Operations\n\nAll arithmetic operations return new matrices; they do not mutate the original.\n\n### add(other)\n\nMatrix addition.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `other` - Matrix with matching dimensions\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix = this + other\n\n**Throws:** If dimensions don't match\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet a = from_rows([[1, 2], [3, 4]]);\nlet b = from_rows([[5, 6], [7, 8]]);\nlet c = a.add(b);\nprint(c.get(0, 0)); // 6\nprint(c.get(1, 1)); // 12\n```\n\n### sub(other)\n\nMatrix subtraction.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `other` - Matrix with matching dimensions\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix = this - other\n\n**Throws:** If dimensions don't match\n\n### mul(other)\n\nMatrix multiplication.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `other` - Matrix where this.cols == other.rows\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix (this.rows x other.cols)\n\n**Throws:** If dimensions are incompatible\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet a = from_rows([[1, 2], [3, 4]]);\nlet b = from_rows([[5, 6], [7, 8]]);\nlet c = a.mul(b);\n// [[1*5+2*7, 1*6+2*8], [3*5+4*7, 3*6+4*8]]\n// [[19, 22], [43, 50]]\n```\n\n### scale(scalar)\n\nScalar multiplication.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `scalar: f64` - Value to multiply each element by\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix = this * scalar\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = from_rows([[1, 2], [3, 4]]);\nlet scaled = m.scale(2.0);\nprint(scaled.get(0, 0)); // 2.0\nprint(scaled.get(1, 1)); // 8.0\n```\n\n### negate()\n\nNegate all elements.\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix = -this\n\n### hadamard(other)\n\nElement-wise multiplication (Hadamard product).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `other` - Matrix with matching dimensions\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix where each element = this[r,c] * other[r,c]\n\n**Throws:** If dimensions don't match\n\n---\n\n## Linear Algebra\n\n### transpose()\n\nReturns the transpose of the matrix.\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix with rows and columns swapped\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = from_rows([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]);\nlet t = m.transpose();\nprint(t.rows); // 3\nprint(t.cols); // 2\nprint(t.get(2, 0)); // 3\n```\n\n### trace()\n\nSum of diagonal elements. Requires a square matrix.\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Sum of diagonal elements\n\n**Throws:** If matrix is not square\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = from_rows([[1, 2], [3, 4]]);\nprint(m.trace()); // 5.0\n```\n\n### det()\n\nComputes the determinant. Requires a square matrix. Uses optimized formulas for 1x1, 2x2, and 3x3 matrices, and cofactor expansion for larger sizes.\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Determinant\n\n**Throws:** If matrix is not square\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = from_rows([[1, 2], [3, 4]]);\nprint(m.det()); // -2.0\n```\n\n### inverse()\n\nComputes the matrix inverse using Gauss-Jordan elimination with partial pivoting.\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix = this^(-1)\n\n**Throws:** If matrix is not square or is singular\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows, identity } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = from_rows([[1, 2], [3, 4]]);\nlet inv = m.inverse();\nlet product = m.mul(inv);\n// product is approximately identity(2)\n```\n\n### norm()\n\nComputes the Frobenius norm: sqrt(sum of squares of all elements).\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Frobenius norm\n\n```hemlock\nimport { identity } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet I = identity(3);\nprint(I.norm()); // ~1.732 (sqrt(3))\n```\n\n### dot(other)\n\nElement-wise dot product (sum of element-wise products). Matrices must have matching dimensions.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `other` - Matrix with matching dimensions\n\n**Returns:** `f64` - Dot product\n\n**Throws:** If dimensions don't match\n\n---\n\n## Utility Methods\n\n### map(f)\n\nApply a function to each element, returning a new matrix.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `f` - Function taking (value, row, col) and returning the new value\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix with transformed elements\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = from_rows([[1, 2], [3, 4]]);\nlet doubled = m.map(fn(val, r, c) { return val * 2; });\nprint(doubled.get(0, 0)); // 2.0\n```\n\n### equals(other, epsilon?)\n\nCheck if two matrices are equal within a tolerance.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `other` - Matrix to compare against\n- `epsilon: f64` - Tolerance (default: 1e-10)\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - true if all elements differ by at most epsilon\n\n### submatrix(r1, c1, r2, c2)\n\nExtract a submatrix from row r1 to r2 (exclusive) and col c1 to c2 (exclusive).\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `r1: i32` - Start row (inclusive)\n- `c1: i32` - Start column (inclusive)\n- `r2: i32` - End row (exclusive)\n- `c2: i32` - End column (exclusive)\n\n**Returns:** New Matrix containing the specified region\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\nlet m = from_rows([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]]);\nlet sub = m.submatrix(0, 0, 2, 2);\n// [[1, 2]\n// [4, 5]]\n```\n\n### to_string()\n\nReturns a human-readable string representation.\n\n**Returns:** `string` - Formatted matrix string\n\n---\n\n## Standalone Functions\n\n### solve(A, b)\n\nSolve a linear system Ax = b using Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `A` - Square coefficient matrix (NxN)\n- `b` - Column vector (Nx1)\n\n**Returns:** Column vector x (Nx1) such that Ax = b\n\n**Throws:** If A is not square, b has wrong dimensions, or the system is singular\n\n```hemlock\nimport { from_rows, col_vector, solve } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\n// Solve: 2x + y = 5, x + 3y = 10\nlet A = from_rows([[2, 1], [1, 3]]);\nlet b = col_vector([5, 10]);\nlet x = solve(A, b);\nprint(x.get(0, 0)); // 1.0\nprint(x.get(1, 0)); // 3.0\n```\n\n---\n\n## Complete Example\n\n```hemlock\nimport {\n Matrix, from_rows, identity,\n col_vector, solve, diagonal\n} from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\n// Create a 3x3 matrix\nlet A = from_rows([\n [2, 1, 0],\n [1, 3, 1],\n [0, 1, 2]\n]);\n\n// Basic properties\nprint(\"Trace: \" + A.trace());\nprint(\"Det: \" + A.det());\n\n// Matrix arithmetic\nlet B = identity(3);\nlet C = A.add(B.scale(2.0));\nprint(\"A + 2I:\");\nprint(C.to_string());\n\n// Solve linear system Ax = b\nlet b = col_vector([4, 10, 6]);\nlet x = solve(A, b);\nprint(\"Solution x:\");\nprint(x.to_string());\n\n// Verify: A * x should equal b\nlet check = A.mul(x);\nprint(\"A * x:\");\nprint(check.to_string());\n\n// Inverse\nlet inv = A.inverse();\nlet product = A.mul(inv);\nprint(\"A * A^-1 is identity: \" + product.equals(identity(3)));\n```\n\n---\n\n## Implementation Notes\n\n- All matrices store elements as `f64` internally\n- Operations return new matrices (immutable style)\n- Determinant uses cofactor expansion (efficient for small matrices, O(n!) for large)\n- Inverse and solve use Gauss-Jordan elimination with partial pivoting for numerical stability\n- Equality comparison uses a configurable epsilon tolerance (default 1e-10)\n- Row-major storage order\n\n---\n\n## Error Handling\n\nMatrix operations throw descriptive error messages:\n\n```hemlock\nimport { Matrix, from_rows } from \"@stdlib/matrix\";\n\n// Dimension mismatch\ntry {\n let a = Matrix(2, 3);\n let b = Matrix(3, 2);\n a.add(b); // throws: dimensions must match\n} catch (e) {\n print(e);\n}\n\n// Singular matrix\ntry {\n let singular = from_rows([[1, 2], [2, 4]]);\n singular.inverse(); // throws: singular\n} catch (e) {\n print(e);\n}\n\n// Out of bounds\ntry {\n let m = Matrix(2, 2);\n m.get(5, 0); // throws: index out of bounds\n} catch (e) {\n print(e);\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\nRun the matrix module tests:\n\n```bash\n# Run all matrix tests\nmake test | grep stdlib_matrix\n\n# Or run individual test\n./hemlock tests/stdlib_matrix/test_basic.hml\n```\n\n---\n\n## License\n\nPart of the Hemlock standard library.\n"}, "Bibliothèque standard -> mmap": {"id": "stdlib-mmap", "content": "# Hemlock Memory-Mapped File I/O Module\n\nA standard library module providing memory-mapped file I/O for high-performance data access in Hemlock.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe mmap module maps files directly into process memory, enabling:\n\n- **Zero-copy file access** - Read/write file data without explicit read/write syscalls\n- **Kernel-managed caching** - The OS page cache handles buffering automatically\n- **Shared memory** - Multiple processes or tasks can share mapped regions\n- **Anonymous mappings** - Large temporary memory allocations backed by the OS\n- **Random access** - Efficient random access patterns on large files\n\nAll mapped regions are returned as raw pointers (`ptr`) and accessed via `ptr_read_*`/`ptr_write_*` builtins.\n\n## Usage\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open, mmap_close, mmap_size } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet p = mmap_open(\"data.bin\", \"r\");\nlet size = mmap_size(p);\n\n// Read first 4 bytes as i32\nlet val = ptr_read_i32(p);\nprint(val);\n\nmmap_close(p);\n```\n\nOr use the high-level wrapper:\n\n```hemlock\nimport { MappedFile } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet f = MappedFile(\"data.bin\", \"r\");\nprint(\"Size: \" + f.size);\nlet byte = f.read_u8(0);\nf.close();\n```\n\n---\n\n## Core Functions\n\n### mmap_open(path, mode?)\n\nMaps a file into memory.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `path: string` - Path to the file to map\n- `mode: string` - Access mode: `\"r\"` (read-only, default) or `\"rw\"` (read-write)\n\n**Returns:** `ptr` - Pointer to the mapped region, or `null` on failure\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open, mmap_close } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\n// Read-only mapping (default)\nlet p = mmap_open(\"config.bin\");\n\n// Read-write mapping\nlet p2 = mmap_open(\"output.bin\", \"rw\");\n\nmmap_close(p);\nmmap_close(p2);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- The file must exist and be non-empty\n- Read-write mode maps with `MAP_SHARED`, so changes are visible to other processes\n- The underlying file descriptor is managed automatically\n\n### mmap_open_anon(size)\n\nCreates an anonymous memory mapping not backed by any file.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `size: i32|i64` - Size of the mapping in bytes (must be positive)\n\n**Returns:** `ptr` - Pointer to the mapped region, or `null` on failure\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open_anon, mmap_close } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\n// Allocate 1MB of anonymous memory\nlet p = mmap_open_anon(1048576);\nptr_write_i32(p, 42);\nprint(ptr_read_i32(p)); // 42\nmmap_close(p);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- Anonymous mappings are always read-write\n- Memory is zero-initialized by the kernel\n- Useful for large allocations where you want OS-level memory management\n\n### mmap_sync(ptr)\n\nFlushes changes in a read-write mapped region to the underlying file on disk.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `ptr: ptr` - Pointer to a mapped region (must have been returned by `mmap_open`)\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - `true` on success, `false` on failure\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open, mmap_sync, mmap_close } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet p = mmap_open(\"data.bin\", \"rw\");\nptr_write_i32(p, 999);\nmmap_sync(p); // Ensure write is flushed to disk\nmmap_close(p);\n```\n\n### mmap_close(ptr)\n\nUnmaps a memory-mapped region and releases all associated resources.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `ptr: ptr` - Pointer to a mapped region\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - `true` on success, `false` on failure\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open, mmap_close } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet p = mmap_open(\"data.bin\");\n// ... use the mapping ...\nmmap_close(p); // Always close when done\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- For file-backed mappings, the underlying file descriptor is closed automatically\n- Accessing the pointer after `mmap_close` is undefined behavior\n\n### mmap_size(ptr)\n\nReturns the size in bytes of a mapped region.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `ptr: ptr` - Pointer to a mapped region\n\n**Returns:** `i64` - Size of the mapping in bytes\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open, mmap_size, mmap_close } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet p = mmap_open(\"data.bin\");\nlet size = mmap_size(p);\nprint(\"File size: \" + size + \" bytes\");\nmmap_close(p);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Advanced Functions\n\n### mmap_advise(ptr, advice)\n\nProvides usage hints to the kernel to optimize access patterns via `madvise()`.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `ptr: ptr` - Pointer to a mapped region\n- `advice: i32` - One of the `MADV_*` constants\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - `true` on success, `false` on failure\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open, mmap_advise, mmap_close, MADV_SEQUENTIAL } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet p = mmap_open(\"large_log.bin\");\nmmap_advise(p, MADV_SEQUENTIAL); // Hint: we'll read sequentially\n// ... read through the file ...\nmmap_close(p);\n```\n\n### mmap_protect(ptr, prot)\n\nChanges the memory protection flags on a mapped region via `mprotect()`.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `ptr: ptr` - Pointer to a mapped region\n- `prot: i32` - Bitwise OR of `PROT_*` constants\n\n**Returns:** `bool` - `true` on success, `false` on failure\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open, mmap_protect, mmap_close, PROT_READ, PROT_NONE } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet p = mmap_open(\"secret.bin\", \"rw\");\n// ... read/write data ...\n\n// Make the region inaccessible (guard page)\nmmap_protect(p, PROT_NONE);\n\n// Restore read access\nmmap_protect(p, PROT_READ);\n\nmmap_close(p);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Constants\n\n### Protection Flags (PROT_*)\n\n| Constant | Description |\n|----------|-------------|\n| `PROT_NONE` | No access allowed |\n| `PROT_READ` | Read access |\n| `PROT_WRITE` | Write access |\n| `PROT_EXEC` | Execute access |\n\n### Madvise Hints (MADV_*)\n\n| Constant | Description |\n|----------|-------------|\n| `MADV_NORMAL` | No special treatment (default) |\n| `MADV_SEQUENTIAL` | Expect sequential page references |\n| `MADV_RANDOM` | Expect random page references |\n| `MADV_WILLNEED` | Pages will be needed soon (prefetch) |\n| `MADV_DONTNEED` | Pages are not needed (allow kernel to free) |\n\n---\n\n## High-Level Wrapper\n\n### MappedFile(path, mode?)\n\nCreates a high-level memory-mapped file object with bounds-checked read/write methods.\n\n**Parameters:**\n- `path: string` - File path to map\n- `mode: string` - `\"r\"` (read-only, default) or `\"rw\"` (read-write)\n\n**Returns:** Object with the following properties and methods:\n\n| Property/Method | Type | Description |\n|----------------|------|-------------|\n| `ptr` | `ptr` | Raw pointer to the mapped region |\n| `size` | `i64` | Size of the mapping in bytes |\n| `read_u8(offset)` | `u8` | Read a byte at offset |\n| `read_i32(offset)` | `i32` | Read an i32 at offset |\n| `read_i64(offset)` | `i64` | Read an i64 at offset |\n| `read_f64(offset)` | `f64` | Read an f64 at offset |\n| `write_u8(offset, val)` | `void` | Write a byte at offset (rw only) |\n| `write_i32(offset, val)` | `void` | Write an i32 at offset (rw only) |\n| `sync()` | `bool` | Flush changes to disk |\n| `advise(hint)` | `bool` | Set access pattern hint |\n| `close()` | `bool` | Unmap and release resources |\n\n```hemlock\nimport { MappedFile, MADV_SEQUENTIAL } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet f = MappedFile(\"measurements.bin\", \"r\");\nf.advise(MADV_SEQUENTIAL);\n\n// Read through the file\nfor (let i = 0; i < f.size; i += 4) {\n let val = f.read_i32(i);\n if (val > 1000) {\n print(\"Found large value at offset \" + i + \": \" + val);\n }\n}\n\nf.close();\n```\n\n---\n\n## Examples\n\n### Reading a Binary File\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open, mmap_size, mmap_close } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet p = mmap_open(\"image.raw\");\nlet size = mmap_size(p);\n\n// Read header (first 4 bytes = width, next 4 = height)\nlet width = ptr_read_i32(p);\nlet height = ptr_read_i32(ptr_offset(p, 4, 1));\nprint(\"Image: \" + width + \"x\" + height);\n\n// Read pixel data starting at offset 8\nfor (let i = 0; i < width * height; i++) {\n let pixel = ptr_read_u8(ptr_offset(p, 8 + i, 1));\n // process pixel...\n}\n\nmmap_close(p);\n```\n\n### Modifying a File In-Place\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open, mmap_size, mmap_sync, mmap_close } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet p = mmap_open(\"counters.bin\", \"rw\");\nlet size = mmap_size(p);\n\n// Increment a counter at offset 0\nlet current = ptr_read_i32(p);\nptr_write_i32(p, current + 1);\n\n// Flush to disk\nmmap_sync(p);\nmmap_close(p);\n```\n\n### Anonymous Shared Memory Between Tasks\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open_anon, mmap_close } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\n// Allocate shared memory region\nlet shared = mmap_open_anon(4096);\n\n// Writer task\nlet writer = spawn(fn() {\n ptr_write_i32(shared, 42);\n});\n\njoin(writer);\n\n// Reader sees the write (shared memory)\nlet val = ptr_read_i32(shared);\nprint(\"Read from shared memory: \" + val); // 42\n\nmmap_close(shared);\n```\n\n### Processing a Large File with Sequential Access Hint\n\n```hemlock\nimport { mmap_open, mmap_size, mmap_advise, mmap_close, MADV_SEQUENTIAL } from \"@stdlib/mmap\";\n\nlet p = mmap_open(\"access.log\");\nlet size = mmap_size(p);\n\n// Tell the kernel we'll read sequentially\nmmap_advise(p, MADV_SEQUENTIAL);\n\n// Process file byte by byte\nlet line_count = 0;\nfor (let i: i64 = 0; i < size; i++) {\n let byte = ptr_read_u8(ptr_offset(p, i, 1));\n if (byte == 10) { // newline\n line_count++;\n }\n}\nprint(\"Lines: \" + line_count);\n\nmmap_close(p);\n```\n\n---\n\n## When to Use mmap\n\n**Use mmap when:**\n- Reading/writing large files where random access is needed\n- Sharing data between processes or tasks\n- Processing binary file formats (headers, records, etc.)\n- You want the OS to handle caching and paging\n\n**Use regular file I/O (`@stdlib/fs`) when:**\n- Reading entire small files as strings\n- Appending to log files\n- Line-by-line text processing\n- Portability is more important than performance\n\n---\n\n## See Also\n\n- **Filesystem module** (`@stdlib/fs`) - Regular file I/O operations\n- **Memory management** - `alloc()`, `free()`, `ptr_read_*`, `ptr_write_*` builtins\n- **Atomic module** (`@stdlib/atomic`) - Atomic operations for shared memory synchronization\n\n---\n\n## License\n\nPart of the Hemlock standard library.\n"}, "Bibliothèque standard -> net": {"id": "stdlib-net", "content": "# @stdlib/net - Networking Module\n\nTCP/UDP networking module providing ergonomic wrappers over raw socket builtins.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe `@stdlib/net` module provides high-level networking abstractions for TCP and UDP communication:\n\n- **TcpListener** - TCP server socket\n- **TcpStream** - TCP client connection\n- **UdpSocket** - UDP datagram socket\n- **Helper functions** - DNS resolution and utilities\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### TCP Echo Server\n\n```hemlock\nimport { TcpListener } from \"@stdlib/net\";\n\nasync fn handle_client(stream) {\n defer stream.close();\n\n let data = stream.read(1024);\n stream.write(data); // Echo back\n}\n\nlet listener = TcpListener(\"0.0.0.0\", 8080);\ndefer listener.close();\n\nwhile (true) {\n let stream = listener.accept();\n spawn(handle_client, stream); // Handle concurrently\n}\n```\n\n### TCP Client\n\n```hemlock\nimport { TcpStream } from \"@stdlib/net\";\n\nlet stream = TcpStream(\"example.com\", 80);\ndefer stream.close();\n\nstream.write(\"GET / HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: example.com\\r\\n\\r\\n\");\nlet response = stream.read(4096);\n```\n\n### UDP Socket\n\n```hemlock\nimport { UdpSocket } from \"@stdlib/net\";\n\nlet sock = UdpSocket(\"0.0.0.0\", 5000);\ndefer sock.close();\n\n// Receive datagram\nlet packet = sock.recv_from(1024);\nprint(\"Received from \" + packet.address + \":\" + typeof(packet.port));\n\n// Send reply\nsock.send_to(packet.address, packet.port, \"Reply\");\n```\n\n---\n\n## API Reference\n\n### TcpListener\n\nTCP server socket for accepting incoming connections.\n\n#### Constructor\n\n**`TcpListener(address: string, port: i32) -> TcpListener`**\n\nCreates a TCP server socket bound to `address:port` and starts listening.\n\n- Automatically sets `SO_REUSEADDR` to avoid \"Address already in use\" errors\n- Default backlog of 128 pending connections\n- Throws exception on bind failure\n\n```hemlock\nlet listener = TcpListener(\"127.0.0.1\", 8080);\nlet listener2 = TcpListener(\"0.0.0.0\", 9000); // Listen on all interfaces\n```\n\n#### Methods\n\n**`accept() -> TcpStream`**\n\nBlocks until a client connects, returns TcpStream for the connection.\n\n```hemlock\nlet stream = listener.accept();\ndefer stream.close();\n```\n\n**`close() -> null`**\n\nCloses the listener socket. Idempotent (safe to call multiple times).\n\n```hemlock\nlistener.close();\n```\n\n#### Properties\n\n- `address: string` - Bound address\n- `port: i32` - Bound port\n\n---\n\n### TcpStream\n\nTCP connection stream for bidirectional data transfer.\n\n#### Constructors\n\n**`TcpStream(address: string, port: i32) -> TcpStream`**\n\nConnects to a TCP server at `address:port`.\n\n- Performs DNS resolution if hostname is provided\n- Throws exception on connection failure\n\n```hemlock\nlet stream = TcpStream(\"example.com\", 80);\nlet stream2 = TcpStream(\"192.168.1.1\", 9000);\n```\n\n**`_TcpStream_from_socket(sock: Socket) -> TcpStream`**\n\nInternal constructor used by `TcpListener.accept()`. Creates TcpStream from existing socket.\n\n#### Methods\n\n**`read(size: i32) -> buffer`**\n\nReads up to `size` bytes from the stream. Returns buffer with received data.\n\n- Returns empty buffer (length 0) on EOF\n- May return less than `size` bytes\n\n```hemlock\nlet data = stream.read(1024);\nprint(\"Received \" + typeof(data.length) + \" bytes\");\n```\n\n**`read_all() -> buffer`**\n\nReads all available data from the stream (up to 64KB).\n\n- Reads in 4KB chunks until no more data is immediately available\n- Useful for reading complete messages\n\n```hemlock\nlet all_data = stream.read_all();\n```\n\n**`read_line() -> string`**\n\nReads until newline (`\\n`) and returns as string.\n\n**Note:** Current implementation is simplified. Future versions will properly handle line buffering.\n\n**`write(data: string | buffer) -> i32`**\n\nWrites `data` to the stream. Returns number of bytes written.\n\n```hemlock\nlet sent = stream.write(\"Hello, server!\");\nlet buf = buffer(10);\nlet sent2 = stream.write(buf);\n```\n\n**`write_line(line: string) -> i32`**\n\nWrites `line` followed by newline (`\\n`). Returns number of bytes written.\n\n```hemlock\nstream.write_line(\"GET / HTTP/1.1\");\nstream.write_line(\"Host: example.com\");\n```\n\n**`set_timeout(seconds: f64) -> null`**\n\nSets read/write timeout in seconds. Supports fractional seconds.\n\n```hemlock\nstream.set_timeout(5.0); // 5 second timeout\nstream.set_timeout(0.5); // 500ms timeout\n```\n\n**`close() -> null`**\n\nCloses the stream. Idempotent.\n\n```hemlock\nstream.close();\n```\n\n#### Properties\n\n- `peer_addr: string` - Remote address (or null for client before connection)\n- `peer_port: i32` - Remote port\n\n---\n\n### UdpSocket\n\nUDP datagram socket for connectionless communication.\n\n#### Constructor\n\n**`UdpSocket(address: string, port: i32) -> UdpSocket`**\n\nCreates a UDP socket bound to `address:port`.\n\n- Bind to `\"0.0.0.0\"` to listen on all interfaces\n- Bind to port `0` to let OS assign a random port\n\n```hemlock\nlet sock = UdpSocket(\"0.0.0.0\", 5000); // Server\nlet sock2 = UdpSocket(\"0.0.0.0\", 0); // Client (any port)\n```\n\n#### Methods\n\n**`send_to(dest_addr: string, dest_port: i32, data: string | buffer) -> i32`**\n\nSends datagram to `dest_addr:dest_port`. Returns number of bytes sent.\n\n```hemlock\nlet sent = sock.send_to(\"192.168.1.100\", 9000, \"Hello UDP!\");\n```\n\n**`recv_from(size: i32) -> { data: buffer, address: string, port: i32 }`**\n\nReceives datagram up to `size` bytes. Returns object with:\n- `data: buffer` - Received data\n- `address: string` - Source IP address\n- `port: i32` - Source port\n\n```hemlock\nlet packet = sock.recv_from(1024);\nprint(\"From \" + packet.address + \":\" + typeof(packet.port));\nprint(\"Data: \" + typeof(packet.data.length) + \" bytes\");\n```\n\n**`set_timeout(seconds: f64) -> null`**\n\nSets receive timeout in seconds.\n\n```hemlock\nsock.set_timeout(2.0); // 2 second timeout\n```\n\n**`close() -> null`**\n\nCloses the socket. Idempotent.\n\n```hemlock\nsock.close();\n```\n\n#### Properties\n\n- `address: string` - Bound address\n- `port: i32` - Bound port\n\n---\n\n## Helper Functions\n\n### resolve\n\n**`resolve(hostname: string) -> string`**\n\nResolves hostname to IPv4 address.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { resolve } from \"@stdlib/net\";\n\nlet ip = resolve(\"localhost\"); // \"127.0.0.1\"\nlet ip2 = resolve(\"example.com\"); // \"93.184.216.34\"\n```\n\n### is_ipv4\n\n**`is_ipv4(address: string) -> bool`**\n\nChecks if `address` is a valid IPv4 address format.\n\n**Note:** Current implementation is simplified. Returns true for basic validation.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { is_ipv4 } from \"@stdlib/net\";\n\nprint(is_ipv4(\"127.0.0.1\")); // true\nprint(is_ipv4(\"example.com\")); // false (simplified check)\n```\n\n### parse_address\n\n**`parse_address(addr_str: string) -> { host: string, port: i32 } | null`**\n\nParses `\"host:port\"` string into components.\n\n**Note:** Current implementation returns placeholder port value. Future versions will properly parse port numbers.\n\n```hemlock\nimport { parse_address } from \"@stdlib/net\";\n\nlet parts = parse_address(\"example.com:8080\");\nif (parts != null) {\n print(\"Host: \" + parts.host);\n print(\"Port: \" + typeof(parts.port));\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Common Patterns\n\n### Async Echo Server\n\n```hemlock\nimport { TcpListener } from \"@stdlib/net\";\n\nasync fn handle_client(stream) {\n defer stream.close();\n\n while (true) {\n let data = stream.read(1024);\n if (data.length == 0) {\n break;
